title: no-unsafe-build-features
description: >-
  A # syntax= line makes BuildKit run a container as your Dockerfile frontend. Which frontends are safe to use, and why RUN --network=host and --security=insecure weaken the build.
---

A `# syntax=` line at the top of a Dockerfile names a container image. BuildKit pulls that image and runs it as the frontend that turns your Dockerfile into a build. Whatever you name there runs as part of your build. This rule reports a `# syntax=` line that selects a frontend outside the official set. It trusts `docker/dockerfile` and `docker/dockerfile-upstream` on Docker Hub, with any tag, so `docker/dockerfile:1` and `docker/dockerfile:1.7-labs` pass. A third-party frontend pinned by digest, such as `registry.example.com/team/frontend@sha256:…`, passes too, because you reviewed one exact artifact. A registry-qualified look-alike such as `ghcr.io/docker/dockerfile` is reported. BuildKit reads the directive only from the comment lines at the very top of the file. A `# syntax=` line after a blank line, a plain comment or an instruction does nothing, and the rule ignores it.

The rule also reports `RUN --security=insecure` and `RUN --network=host`. Both flags remove isolation from one build step. The rule reads only the flags that come right after `RUN`, so `RUN docker run --network=host app` passes.

## What the rule catches

```dockerfile title="Dockerfile with a third-party frontend and two RUN steps that drop isolation"
# syntax=ghcr.io/example/dockerfile-frontend:latest
FROM debian:12-slim
RUN --security=insecure make install
RUN --network=host ./fetch-assets.sh
```

Scanning this file reports:

```text
⚠ WARN [docker-doctor/no-unsafe-build-features]
  Dockerfile selects BuildKit frontend 'ghcr.io/example/dockerfile-frontend:latest'. A frontend runs with access to the build, so an untrusted one can read or change what it builds.
```

## Why it matters

A frontend is not a parser that reads your file and stays out of the way. It is a container that BuildKit runs during the build, and it talks to BuildKit over an API. Two BuildKit advisories show what that costs when the frontend is not one you trust. [CVE-2026-33747](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/security/advisories/GHSA-4c29-8rgm-jvjj) let a custom frontend craft an API message that wrote files outside BuildKit's state directory. The advisory says the issue needs an untrusted frontend set with `#syntax` or `--build-arg BUILDKIT_SYNTAX`, and that a well-known frontend image such as `docker/dockerfile` is not affected. The fix shipped in BuildKit v0.28.1. [CVE-2026-61711](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/security/advisories/GHSA-7236-3392-c5c6) let a custom frontend send a crafted build request that turned off Seccomp and AppArmor for the build container, even when the user had not allowed the `security.insecure` entitlement. The fix shipped in BuildKit v0.31.1. The advisory's workaround is to use only frontends from trusted providers.

The RUN flags are the same trade made on purpose. `--security=insecure` runs the step without the sandbox, and `--network=host` shares the host's network with it. A build step that needs either one can reach more of the machine than a normal step can, so each one deserves a second look.

## How to fix it

Use the official `docker/dockerfile` frontend, or pin a third-party one by digest after reviewing it. Remove --security=insecure and --network=host unless the build truly needs them.

```dockerfile title="Dockerfile with the official frontend and a sandboxed RUN step"
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
FROM python:3.12-slim
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/pip pip install -r requirements.txt
```

Use the official frontend unless you have a reason not to:

```dockerfile
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
```

If you need a third-party frontend, review it and pin the exact image by digest. A tag can move, a digest cannot.

BuildKit lets you set a frontend outside the Dockerfile too, with `--build-arg BUILDKIT_SYNTAX=…`. That value is not in the file, so this rule cannot see it. Check your build scripts and CI for it.

`--security=insecure` and `--network=host` need the matching entitlements on the builder (`--allow security.insecure`, `--allow network.host`). If a build step needs one of them, keep it in a dedicated build and leave it out of the Dockerfile you publish.

## Rule details

- **Rule key** — `docker-doctor/no-unsafe-build-features`
- **Category** — Security
- **Default severity** — `warning`
- **Applies to** — Dockerfiles

Explain this rule from the CLI:

```bash
npx @docker-doctor/cli@latest rules explain docker-doctor/no-unsafe-build-features
```

Change its severity — or turn it off — in your [config file](/docs/reference/configuration):

```ts
// docker-doctor.config.ts
export default {
  rules: {
    "docker-doctor/no-unsafe-build-features": "off",
  },
};
```

Severity affects the [health score](/docs/reference/scoring): `error` findings cost more points than `warning`, and `info` costs the least.
